chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khazzaz, from Harun ibn Harjah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn, knowing his right, seeking the Face of Allah the Exalted and the Hereafter?' He said to him, 'O Harun! Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, seeking the Face of Allah and the Hereafter, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sins and what followed.' Then he said to me three times, 'Did I not swear to you? Did I not swear to you? Did I not swear to you?'

key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (seeking His pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with sincerity?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) profound assurance that visiting Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) grave with gnosis (ma'rifah) of his rights and sincere intention (iradah) for the Hereafter guarantees complete forgiveness of sins. The Imam’s triple repetition of 'Did I not swear to you?' underscores the certainty and weight of this divine promise, linking the physical act of ziyarah to spiritual purification. This tradition highlights the Shia theological view that the Ahl al-Bayt serve as intercessors and focal points for divine mercy, reinforcing the eschatological significance of their graves.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Abān Al-Aḥmar, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain Al-Khazzāz, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “May I sacrifice myself for you! What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights, seeking nearness with Allāh, the Exalted, and hoping for (the blessings of) the Hereafter?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “O Hārūn! I swear to Allāh that Allāh will forgive all of the past and future sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights, seeking nearness with Allāh, and hoping for (the blessings of) the Hereafter.” Then Imam (a.s.) added, “Did I not swear to Allāh for you?! Did I not swear to Allāh for you?! Did I not swear to Allāh for you?!”
